"""`GET /admin/workspace-config` — the read-only retention + sign-in allowlist readout."""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections.abc import Callable, Iterator
from typing import Any

import pytest
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

from backend.app.core.config import get_settings
from backend.app.db.session import get_db
from backend.app.main import app

URL = "/api/v1/admin/workspace-config"


@pytest.fixture
def client(db_session: Any) -> Iterator[TestClient]:
    app.dependency_overrides[get_db] = lambda: db_session
    try:
        yield TestClient(app)
    finally:
        app.dependency_overrides.clear()


@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
def _fresh_settings() -> Iterator[None]:
    get_settings.cache_clear()
    yield
    get_settings.cache_clear()


def _set(monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch, **env: str) -> None:
    for key, value in env.items():
        monkeypatch.setenv(key, value)
    get_settings.cache_clear()


def _by_variable(body: dict[str, Any], key: str) -> dict[str, dict[str, Any]]:
    return {row["variable"]: row for row in body[key]}


def test_reports_the_configured_retention_clocks(
    client: TestClient, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch
) -> None:
    _set(
        monkeypatch,
        SAMPLE_FAILURES_RETENTION_DAYS="7",
        AUDIT_RETENTION_DAYS="400",
        OTP_CODES_RETENTION_HOURS="12",
    )
    body = client.get(URL).json()
    retention = _by_variable(body, "retention")
    samples = retention["SAMPLE_FAILURES_RETENTION_DAYS"]
    assert (samples["value"], samples["unit"]) == (7, "days")
    assert retention["AUDIT_RETENTION_DAYS"]["value"] == 400
    codes = retention["OTP_CODES_RETENTION_HOURS"]
    assert (codes["value"], codes["unit"]) == (12, "hours")
    assert all(row["detail"] for row in body["retention"])


def test_allowlist_for_an_unused_mode_is_shown_but_inert(
    client: TestClient, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch
) -> None:
    # OIDC values set with no OIDC issuer configured: no door reads them (ADR 0043), so the
    # readout must not present them as the thing keeping anyone out — or in.
    _set(
        monkeypatch,
        OIDC_ALLOWED_EMAILS="Ada@Example.com, grace@example.com",
        OIDC_ALLOWED_DOMAINS="example.org",
        WORKSPACE_ADMIN_EMAILS="root@example.com",
    )
    body = client.get(URL).json()
    lists = _by_variable(body, "signup_allowlists")
    oidc = lists["OIDC_ALLOWED_EMAILS"]
    assert oidc["values"] == ["ada@example.com", "grace@example.com"]
    assert oidc["active"] is False
    assert lists["OIDC_ALLOWED_DOMAINS"]["values"] == ["example.org"]
    admin = lists["WORKSPACE_ADMIN_EMAILS"]
    # It admits the address AND grants Admin — the guide must never call it role-only.
    assert (admin["values"], admin["active"], admin["grants"]) == (
        ["root@example.com"],
        True,
        "sign_in_and_admin_role",
    )
    # The test stack signs in through the developer bypass, which an OIDC issuer would displace.
    assert (body["sign_in_mode"], body["dev_bypass_active"]) == ("dev_bypass", True)
    assert body["idp_decides_signup"] is False
    assert set(lists) == {
        "OIDC_ALLOWED_EMAILS",
        "OIDC_ALLOWED_DOMAINS",
        "AUTH_OTP_ALLOWED_EMAILS",
        "AUTH_OTP_ALLOWED_DOMAINS",
        "WORKSPACE_ADMIN_EMAILS",
    }
    sign_in = {v: row for v, row in lists.items() if v != "WORKSPACE_ADMIN_EMAILS"}
    assert all(row["grants"] == "sign_in" for row in sign_in.values())


def test_allowlist_is_active_when_its_mode_gates_a_door(
    client: TestClient, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch
) -> None:
    _set(
        monkeypatch,
        OIDC_ISSUER="https://issuer.example.com/",
        OIDC_AUDIENCE="dataq",
        OIDC_ALLOWED_DOMAINS="example.com",
        WORKSPACE_ADMIN_EMAILS="dev@dataq.local",
    )
    body = client.get(URL).json()
    lists = _by_variable(body, "signup_allowlists")
    assert lists["OIDC_ALLOWED_DOMAINS"]["active"] is True
    assert lists["OIDC_ALLOWED_EMAILS"]["active"] is True  # same door, empty list
    assert lists["AUTH_OTP_ALLOWED_EMAILS"]["active"] is False
    assert body["dev_bypass_active"] is False
    assert (body["sign_in_mode"], body["idp_decides_signup"]) == ("oidc", False)
    assert (body["oidc_default_role"], body["otp_default_role"]) == ("member", "member")


def test_oidc_without_an_allowlist_is_reported_as_the_idp_deciding(
    client: TestClient, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch
) -> None:
    # The open-pool posture: OIDC in use, no app-side allowlist. The rows are empty and
    # inactive, which alone would read as "mode not configured" — the opposite of the truth.
    _set(monkeypatch, OIDC_ISSUER="https://issuer.example.com/", OIDC_AUDIENCE="dataq")
    body = client.get(URL).json()
    assert (body["sign_in_mode"], body["idp_decides_signup"]) == ("oidc", True)
    assert _by_variable(body, "signup_allowlists")["OIDC_ALLOWED_EMAILS"]["active"] is False


def test_the_retention_readout_names_every_sweep_that_deletes(client: TestClient) -> None:
    body = client.get(URL).json()
    assert set(_by_variable(body, "retention")) == {
        "SAMPLE_FAILURES_RETENTION_DAYS",
        "AUDIT_RETENTION_DAYS",
        "OTP_CODES_RETENTION_HOURS",
        "ASSET_ORPHAN_RETENTION_DAYS",
    }


def test_the_readout_carries_no_secret_bearing_setting(client: TestClient) -> None:
    body = client.get(URL).json()
    text = str(body).lower()
    for forbidden in ("secret", "password", "token", "client_secret"):
        assert forbidden not in text, forbidden


@pytest.mark.parametrize("role", ["member", "viewer"])
def test_non_admins_are_refused(
    client: TestClient, as_role: Callable[..., tuple[Any, dict[str, str]]], role: str
) -> None:
    _, headers = as_role(role)
    response = client.get(URL, headers=headers)
    assert response.status_code == 403

## Settings — sign-in access (read-only)

The **Sign-in access** card shows the deployment's allowlists exactly as configured — the
values of `OIDC_ALLOWED_EMAILS`, `OIDC_ALLOWED_DOMAINS`, `AUTH_OTP_ALLOWED_EMAILS`,
`AUTH_OTP_ALLOWED_DOMAINS` and `WORKSPACE_ADMIN_EMAILS` — with a worded status per row:

- **Read at sign-in** — a sign-in door on this deployment reads the list.
- **Not read — sign-in mode not configured** — the list has values but its mode is not the
  one this deployment uses, so it admits nobody. Values set for the wrong mode are a
  common reason an expected sign-in is refused; this row makes that visible.
- **Grants the Admin role** — `WORKSPACE_ADMIN_EMAILS`, which never admits anyone by itself
  but grants Admin to whoever it names (see [seed and emergency access](#seed-and-emergency-access)).

card is read-only: these values change only when the deployment's configuration is edited
and the app restarted, and they are identifiers, never secrets. On a local stack signing in
through the developer bypass the card says so, because no allowlist gates anything there.
Day-to-day admission is the [Members](#members) tab.

The **Data retention** card lists each retention clock with the variable that sets it and
what the daily sweep removes when it runs out: failing-row samples and captured cell values
inside stored results (`SAMPLE_FAILURES_RETENTION_DAYS`), audit events
(`AUDIT_RETENTION_DAYS`) and spent sign-in codes (`OTP_CODES_RETENTION_HOURS`). Run and

"""`GET /admin/workspace-config` — the read-only retention + sign-in allowlist readout."""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections.abc import Callable, Iterator
from typing import Any

import pytest
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

from backend.app.core.config import get_settings
from backend.app.db.session import get_db
from backend.app.main import app

URL = "/api/v1/admin/workspace-config"


@pytest.fixture
def client(db_session: Any) -> Iterator[TestClient]:
    app.dependency_overrides[get_db] = lambda: db_session
    try:
        yield TestClient(app)
    finally:
        app.dependency_overrides.clear()


@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
def _fresh_settings() -> Iterator[None]:
    get_settings.cache_clear()
    yield
    get_settings.cache_clear()


def _set(monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch, **env: str) -> None:
    for key, value in env.items():
        monkeypatch.setenv(key, value)
    get_settings.cache_clear()


def _by_variable(body: dict[str, Any], key: str) -> dict[str, dict[str, Any]]:
    return {row["variable"]: row for row in body[key]}


def test_reports_the_configured_retention_clocks(
    client: TestClient, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch
) -> None:
    _set(
        monkeypatch,
        SAMPLE_FAILURES_RETENTION_DAYS="7",
        AUDIT_RETENTION_DAYS="400",
        OTP_CODES_RETENTION_HOURS="12",
    )
    body = client.get(URL).json()
    retention = _by_variable(body, "retention")
    samples = retention["SAMPLE_FAILURES_RETENTION_DAYS"]
    assert (samples["value"], samples["unit"]) == (7, "days")
    assert retention["AUDIT_RETENTION_DAYS"]["value"] == 400
    codes = retention["OTP_CODES_RETENTION_HOURS"]
    assert (codes["value"], codes["unit"]) == (12, "hours")
    assert all(row["detail"] for row in body["retention"])


def test_allowlist_for_an_unused_mode_is_shown_but_inert(
    client: TestClient, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch
) -> None:
    # OIDC values set with no OIDC issuer configured: no door reads them (ADR 0043), so the
    # readout must not present them as the thing keeping anyone out — or in.
    _set(
        monkeypatch,
        OIDC_ALLOWED_EMAILS="Ada@Example.com, grace@example.com",
        OIDC_ALLOWED_DOMAINS="example.org",
        WORKSPACE_ADMIN_EMAILS="root@example.com",
    )
    body = client.get(URL).json()
    lists = _by_variable(body, "signup_allowlists")
    oidc = lists["OIDC_ALLOWED_EMAILS"]
    assert oidc["values"] == ["ada@example.com", "grace@example.com"]
    assert oidc["active"] is False
    assert lists["OIDC_ALLOWED_DOMAINS"]["values"] == ["example.org"]
    admin = lists["WORKSPACE_ADMIN_EMAILS"]
    # It admits the address AND grants Admin — the guide must never call it role-only.
    assert (admin["values"], admin["active"], admin["grants"]) == (
        ["root@example.com"],
        True,
        "sign_in_and_admin_role",
    )
    # The test stack signs in through the developer bypass, which an OIDC issuer would displace.
    assert (body["sign_in_mode"], body["dev_bypass_active"]) == ("dev_bypass", True)
    assert body["idp_decides_signup"] is False
    assert set(lists) == {
        "OIDC_ALLOWED_EMAILS",
        "OIDC_ALLOWED_DOMAINS",
        "AUTH_OTP_ALLOWED_EMAILS",
        "AUTH_OTP_ALLOWED_DOMAINS",
        "WORKSPACE_ADMIN_EMAILS",
    }
    sign_in = {v: row for v, row in lists.items() if v != "WORKSPACE_ADMIN_EMAILS"}
    assert all(row["grants"] == "sign_in" for row in sign_in.values())


def test_allowlist_is_active_when_its_mode_gates_a_door(
    client: TestClient, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch
) -> None:
    _set(
        monkeypatch,
        OIDC_ISSUER="https://issuer.example.com/",
        OIDC_AUDIENCE="dataq",
        OIDC_ALLOWED_DOMAINS="example.com",
        WORKSPACE_ADMIN_EMAILS="dev@dataq.local",
    )
    body = client.get(URL).json()
    lists = _by_variable(body, "signup_allowlists")
    assert lists["OIDC_ALLOWED_DOMAINS"]["active"] is True
    assert lists["OIDC_ALLOWED_EMAILS"]["active"] is True  # same door, empty list
    assert lists["AUTH_OTP_ALLOWED_EMAILS"]["active"] is False
    assert body["dev_bypass_active"] is False
    assert (body["sign_in_mode"], body["idp_decides_signup"]) == ("oidc", False)
    assert (body["oidc_default_role"], body["otp_default_role"]) == ("member", "member")


def test_oidc_without_an_allowlist_is_reported_as_the_idp_deciding(
    client: TestClient, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch
) -> None:
    # The open-pool posture: OIDC in use, no app-side allowlist. The rows are empty and
    # inactive, which alone would read as "mode not configured" — the opposite of the truth.
    _set(monkeypatch, OIDC_ISSUER="https://issuer.example.com/", OIDC_AUDIENCE="dataq")
    body = client.get(URL).json()
    assert (body["sign_in_mode"], body["idp_decides_signup"]) == ("oidc", True)
    assert _by_variable(body, "signup_allowlists")["OIDC_ALLOWED_EMAILS"]["active"] is False


def test_the_retention_readout_names_every_sweep_that_deletes(client: TestClient) -> None:
    body = client.get(URL).json()
    assert set(_by_variable(body, "retention")) == {
        "SAMPLE_FAILURES_RETENTION_DAYS",
        "AUDIT_RETENTION_DAYS",
        "OTP_CODES_RETENTION_HOURS",
        "ASSET_ORPHAN_RETENTION_DAYS",
    }


def test_the_readout_carries_no_secret_bearing_setting(client: TestClient) -> None:
    body = client.get(URL).json()
    text = str(body).lower()
    for forbidden in ("secret", "password", "token", "client_secret"):
        assert forbidden not in text, forbidden


@pytest.mark.parametrize("role", ["member", "viewer"])
def test_non_admins_are_refused(
    client: TestClient, as_role: Callable[..., tuple[Any, dict[str, str]]], role: str
) -> None:
    _, headers = as_role(role)
    response = client.get(URL, headers=headers)
    assert response.status_code == 403

import re,io
p='backend/app/api/v1/admin.py'
s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace('''    #: Whether a sign-in door on THIS deployment reads it. An allowlist for a mode the
    #: deployment does not use admits nobody, so its values are shown but inert.
    active: bool''','''    #: Whether this deployment signs people in through the mode that reads this list. False
    #: means the mode is not in use, so the values are shown but inert. True with an empty
    #: list on an OIDC deployment is the open posture `idp_decides_signup` names.
    active: bool''')
old=s[s.index('    settings = get_settings()\n    active_vars'):s.index('    def _allowlist(')]
s=s.replace(old,'''    settings = get_settings()
    active_vars: set[str] = set()
    if settings.generic_oidc_configured:
        active_vars |= {"OIDC_ALLOWED_EMAILS", "OIDC_ALLOWED_DOMAINS"}
    if settings.otp_auth_configured:
        active_vars |= {"AUTH_OTP_ALLOWED_EMAILS", "AUTH_OTP_ALLOWED_DOMAINS"}

''')
s=s.replace("    membership_service,\n    privacy_settings_service,","    privacy_settings_service,")
open(p,'w').write(s)

# revert the now-unused service helper
p='backend/app/services/membership_service.py'
s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace('''def configured_allowlists(settings: Settings | None = None) -> list[_NamedGate]:
    """The sign-in allowlists a door on THIS deployment reads, each with the env
    vars it came from — the read-only readout Workspace Settings shows.
    """
    return _named_gates(settings or get_settings())


''','')
open(p,'w').write(s)

# tests
p='backend/tests/api/test_admin_workspace_config.py'
s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace('''    # The open-pool posture: OIDC in use, no app-side allowlist. The rows are empty and
    # inactive, which alone would read as "mode not configured" — the opposite of the truth.
    _set(monkeypatch, OIDC_ISSUER="https://issuer.example.com/", OIDC_AUDIENCE="dataq")
    body = client.get(URL).json()
    assert (body["sign_in_mode"], body["idp_decides_signup"]) == ("oidc", True)
    assert _by_variable(body, "signup_allowlists")["OIDC_ALLOWED_EMAILS"]["active"] is False''','''    # The open-pool posture: OIDC in use, no app-side allowlist. The mode IS configured, so
    # its rows stay active (an inactive row would read as "mode not configured" — the
    # opposite of the truth) and the top-level flag names what an empty active list means.
    _set(monkeypatch, OIDC_ISSUER="https://issuer.example.com/", OIDC_AUDIENCE="dataq")
    body = client.get(URL).json()
    assert (body["sign_in_mode"], body["idp_decides_signup"]) == ("oidc", True)
    lists = _by_variable(body, "signup_allowlists")
    assert (lists["OIDC_ALLOWED_EMAILS"]["active"], lists["OIDC_ALLOWED_EMAILS"]["values"]) == (
        True,
        [],
    )
    assert lists["OIDC_ALLOWED_DOMAINS"]["active"] is True
    assert lists["AUTH_OTP_ALLOWED_EMAILS"]["active"] is False


def test_azure_ad_mode_reports_the_tenant_as_the_gate(
    client: TestClient, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch
) -> None:
    _set(
        monkeypatch,
        AZURE_TENANT_ID="11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111",
        AZURE_API_CLIENT_ID="22222222-2222-2222-2222-222222222222",
        OIDC_ALLOWED_DOMAINS="example.com",
    )
    body = client.get(URL).json()
    assert (body["sign_in_mode"], body["idp_decides_signup"]) == ("azure_ad", True)
    lists = _by_variable(body, "signup_allowlists")
    # No app-side allowlist is read in this mode: the OIDC values are shown but inert.
    assert all(
        lists[v]["active"] is False
        for v in (
            "OIDC_ALLOWED_EMAILS",
            "OIDC_ALLOWED_DOMAINS",
            "AUTH_OTP_ALLOWED_EMAILS",
            "AUTH_OTP_ALLOWED_DOMAINS",
        )
    )''')
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run the backend test suite locally against the docker-compose Postgres + Redis.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

# Local infra creds (POSTGRES_USER/PASSWORD/DB) live in the gitignored .env that
# scripts/setup.sh generates.
if [ ! -f .env ]; then
  echo "error: .env not found — run scripts/setup.sh first (it generates the local creds)." >&2
  exit 1
fi
set -a; . ./.env; set +a
: "${POSTGRES_USER:?POSTGRES_USER not set in .env}"
: "${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:?POSTGRES_PASSWORD not set in .env}"

echo "==> ensuring postgres + redis are up (docker compose)…"
docker compose up -d postgres redis >/dev/null
until docker compose exec -T postgres pg_isready -U "$POSTGRES_USER" >/dev/null 2>&1; do
  echo "   waiting for postgres…"; sleep 1
done

# Dedicated test DB, separate from the dev DB. Idempotent.
if ! docker compose exec -T postgres psql -U "$POSTGRES_USER" -tAc \
      "SELECT 1 FROM pg_database WHERE datname='dataq_test'" | grep -q 1; then
  echo "==> creating dataq_test database…"
  docker compose exec -T postgres createdb -U "$POSTGRES_USER" dataq_test
fi

TEST_URL="postgresql+psycopg2://${POSTGRES_USER}:${POSTGRES_PASSWORD}@localhost:5432/dataq_test"
echo "==> running pytest against dataq_test + local redis…"
exec conda run -n dataq --no-capture-output env \
  TEST_DATABASE_URL="$TEST_URL" \
  DATABASE_URL="$TEST_URL" \
  REDIS_URL="redis://localhost:6379/0" \
  DATAQ_E2E=1 \
  python -m pytest backend/tests "$@"

- uses: actions/setup-python@v7
        with:
          python-version: "3.13"
          cache: pip

      - name: Install the package and its tooling
        run: |
          pip install -r packages/dataq-client/requirements-dev.txt
          pip install -e packages/dataq-client

      - name: Generated client matches the committed OpenAPI spec
        # The spec itself is checked against the app in backend-test; a route change must
        # regenerate both (scripts/generate-dataq-client.py).
        run: python scripts/generate-dataq-client.py --check

      - name: Types (hand-written layer)
        run: mypy --config-file packages/dataq-client/pyproject.toml packages/dataq-client/src/dataq_client/client.py packages/dataq-client/src/dataq_client/cli.py

      - name: Tests
        run: pytest -c packages/dataq-client/pyproject.toml -q -p no:cacheprovider packages/dataq-client/tests

  (every non-owned suite is stamped `admin` for them); `effectiveRole()` deleted in
  favour of the server-resolved `me.role`; the suites fetch mounts only once /me is ok.
- openapi.json + generated client regenerated; tests for every case above.

EOF

- Profile makes one small request instead of listing every suite.

=== notifications.md
+- **In-app feed** — a bell in the header with an unread count; every alert also lands in the
+  feed of each user who can see the suite, with read-acks and links to the run and incident.
-HMAC-signed **webhooks** — all

+HMAC-signed **webhooks**, and in the app itself through the **notification feed** behind
+the header bell — all behind one `ResultPublisher` seam, so every channel gets the same
+severity-aware behaviour. Alerts fire from the worker as soon as a run reaches a terminal
+state.
+## In-app notification feed
+
+The bell in the app header is a destination like any other, with two differences: it needs no
+configuration, and it is scoped per person. When a run's outcome passes a suite's alert
+threshold, the same entry is written to the feed of **everyone who can see that suite** — its
+owner, each user it is shared with (at any level, including view-only), and the workspace
+admins. Someone with no access to a suite never sees its alerts; someone granted access later
+sees alerts from that point on, not the history.
+
+- **Badge and feed.** The bell's count is your unread entries, refreshed about once a minute
+  while the tab is visible. Open it for the feed, newest first: each entry names the suite,
+  how many checks breached and the worst tier (or that the run failed to execute), lists the
+  breaching checks by name, and links to the run — and, when an incident is open for it, to
+  the incident on its asset page.
+- **Read state is yours.** Mark an entry read from the feed, or follow its link (which marks
+  it read on the way); **Mark all read** clears the badge. Nobody else's badge changes, and an
+  admin cannot read or clear another person's feed.
+- **Same rules as the outbound channels.** The per-suite threshold, severity routing, dedup and
+  snooze below apply to the feed exactly as to Teams, Slack, email and webhooks. A suite with
+  alerting disabled writes nothing to anyone's feed.
+- **Only check names, never values.** Feed entries are built from the same redacted report the
+  other channels send and carry counts and check names only; no observed value or sample row
+  ever reaches the feed, whatever the suite's masking policy.
+- **An entry can outlive its run.** If the run it points at is later deleted with its suite,
+  the entry stays and says *Run no longer available* instead of offering a dead link.
+- **Keyboard and screen reader.** The bell's name carries the unread count; the feed is a
+  dialog whose entries are ordinary links and buttons; a rise in the count while the feed is
+  closed is announced.
+
+The feed is also readable over the API — `GET /notifications` (paged, `unread_only=`, with
+`X-Total-Count`), `GET /notifications/unread_count`, `POST /notifications/{id}/read` and
+`POST /notifications/read_all` — always for the caller's own entries only. Connection
+poll-health and pipeline-overdue signals go to the outbound channels only; they have no suite
+to scope a feed by.
+

+severity-aware behaviour. Alerts fire from the worker as soon as a run reaches a terminal
+state.
+## In-app notification feed
+
+The bell in the app header is a destination like any other, with two differences: it needs no
+configuration, and it is scoped per person. When a run's outcome passes a suite's alert
+threshold, the same entry is written to the feed of **everyone who can see that suite** — its
+owner, each user it is shared with (at any level, including view-only), and the workspace
+admins. Someone with no access to a suite never sees its alerts; someone granted access later
+sees alerts from that point on, not the history.
+
+- **Badge and feed.** The bell's count is your unread entries, refreshed about once a minute
+  while the tab is visible. Open it for the feed, newest first: each entry names the suite,
+  how many checks breached and the worst tier (or that the run failed to execute), lists the
+  breaching checks by name, and links to the run — and, when an incident is open for it, to
+  the incident on its asset page.
+- **Read state is yours.** Mark an entry read from the feed, or follow its link (which marks
+  it read on the way); **Mark all read** clears the badge. Nobody else's badge changes, and an
+  admin cannot read or clear another person's feed.
+- **Same rules as the outbound channels.** The per-suite threshold, severity routing, dedup and
+  snooze below apply to the feed exactly as to Teams, Slack, email and webhooks. A suite with
+  alerting disabled writes nothing to anyone's feed.
+- **Only check names, never values.** Feed entries are built from the same redacted report the
+  other channels send and carry counts and check names only; no observed value or sample row
+  ever reaches the feed, whatever the suite's masking policy.
+- **An entry can outlive its run.** If the run it points at is later deleted with its suite,
+  the entry stays and says *Run no longer available* instead of offering a dead link.
+- **Keyboard and screen reader.** The bell's name carries the unread count; the feed is a
+  dialog whose entries are ordinary links and buttons; a rise in the count while the feed is
+  closed is announced.

+`X-Total-Count`), `GET /notifications/unread_count`, `POST /notifications/{id}/read` and

+poll-health and pipeline-overdue signals go to the outbound channels only; they have no suite
+to scope a feed by.

# Static demo lane

The read-only demo published at `/demo/` on the GitHub Pages site (#2419) is the real
frontend, built with `VITE_DEMO=true` so the API client answers from recorded responses
instead of a backend. Nothing here is committed output: CI records, builds and smoke-tests
it on every run of the `frontend-e2e` job, and a push to `main` publishes the result.

| Step   | Command             | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ------ | ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Record | `pnpm demo:capture` | Visits every route in `routes.ts` (and each tab on it) against the seeded dev-bypass stack and writes the `GET /api/v1` responses to `demo-fixtures.json`.                                       |
| Build  | `pnpm demo:build`   | Builds the SPA for `DEMO_BASE` (default `/DataQ/demo/`) into `dist-demo/`, with the fixtures and a `config.js` that selects no-IdP mode.                                                         |
| Smoke  | `pnpm demo:smoke`   | Serves `marketing/` + `dist-demo/` the way GitHub Pages does (`pages-server.mjs`) and drives the built files: every route renders from the recording alone, deep links work, writes are refused. |

Locally, record against the docs capture stack so your own workspace is never the source:

```bash
scripts/docs/capture-stack.sh start
cd frontend
E2E_DEMO_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:3001 pnpm demo:capture
pnpm demo:build && pnpm demo:smoke
```

## How the capture waits

Each page and tab waits at most 1.5 s for the network to go quiet, then requires the spinner
gate (`settle`) to pass. A polling endpoint or a hung asset therefore costs 1.5 s, not the 5 s
a plain idle wait used to take on every page and tab. Requests still open after the grace are
logged by method and path (`[capture] <route>: network busy past the grace`). Each route has a
hard budget (`ROUTE_BUDGET_MS`); one that exceeds it fails the test naming the route and the
requests still open, instead of running into the test-wide ceiling. Reading a response body is
bounded the same way (10 s, logged by path): a body the page abandoned mid-flight never settles,
and without the bound it held the end of the capture until the test-wide timeout.

## What keeps it from drifting

- **A new route** must be added to `ROUTE_PATTERNS` in `routes.ts`;
  `tests/demo/routeCoverage.test.ts` fails otherwise.
- **A new request on an existing route** is recorded automatically, because the recording is
  remade from the current code on every CI run.
- **A request the recording cannot answer** (a value that changes between record and replay,
  a call that bypasses the shared axios client, an absolute URL that ignores the base path)
  fails the smoke test.
- **Dates** in the recording are moved forward by whole days at replay, so the data reads as
  recent between publishes.

## What the demo does not do

Requests made only after a click that the crawl does not perform (a drawer, a filter, a
download) are not recorded. The demo says so in a notice instead of showing an empty or
wrong view. Every non-`GET` request is refused with a notice that links to the install
guide.

{"body":"## Summary\nIntroduce first-class tags (workspace-shared labels) on the four core entities — `Suite`, `Asset`, `Connection`, `Check` — with tag filters on the list endpoints and tag chips/pickers in the UI.\n\nFeasibility assessed 2026-07-17: fully greenfield — no tag concept exists in the data model today (every \"tag\" hit in the frontend is the antd `\u003cTag\u003e` UI component). Skill "code-review" completed (forked execution).

Result:
Review of PR #2538 (`feat(ui): in-app notification center`, head `c239ba5a`) at low effort across the 8 inline angles. Eight findings survived dedup; all were posted to the PR (7 inline review comments, 1 PR-level comment because `capture.spec.ts` is outside the diff and GitHub refuses an inline anchor there).

```json
[
  {
    "file": "frontend/src/components/assets/IncidentsPanel.tsx",
    "line": 91,
    "summary": "`initialIncidentId` is read only at mount (`useState(initialIncidentId)`), so a changed `?incident=` deep link never opens the second incident.",
    "failure_scenario": "User is on /assets/A (drawer closed or showing incident X), opens the bell and follows a notification whose incident_link is /assets/A?incident=Y. AssetDetailBody/IncidentsPanel stay mounted, useState keeps its first value, the evidence drawer for Y never opens and the click appears to do nothing. Closing the drawer also leaves ?incident= in the URL so refresh/back re-opens it. Fix: a useEffect on initialIncidentId (and clear the param on close)."
  },
  {
    "file": "backend/app/services/notification_feed_service.py",
    "line": 78,
    "summary": "A succeeded run whose checks only `error`/`skip` is stored as severity `pass` titled \"all N checks passed\".",
    "failure_scenario": "worst_severity() ignores operational statuses and total_checks counts every status, so with alert_on: always a run where all 3 checks errored (bad SQL / dropped column) yields severity='pass', title '…: all 3 checks passed', body '… — nothing breached.' — a stored confident wrong answer (the #1444 class). email.py:38 has the same pre-existing shape; per CLAUDE.md §11 that is fixed-or-filed, not a disposition."
  },
  {
    "file": "backend/app/db/models.py",
    "line": 892,
    "summary": "`notifications` has no retention or cap: one row per recipient per published run, forever, including read rows.",
    "failure_scenario": "10 users (admins receive every suite) × 40 scheduled suites at alert_on: always every 5 min ≈ 115k rows/day; after a quarter ~10M rows nothing purges (the A8 sweep touches results, not this table), and count_feed/X-Total-Count on every drawer open scans the user's whole partition. Needs a beat-dispatched purge or a bounded fan-out."
  },
  {
    "file": "backend/app/alerting/inapp.py",
    "line": 36,
    "summary": "The publisher commits the worker's shared session mid fan-out — the only ResultPublisher that owns a transaction boundary.",
    "failure_scenario": "publish_run_outcome runs on the run task's long-lived session after sync_incidents_for_run/_usage_run_completed; session.commit() here commits whatever an earlier fail-soft hook or sibling publisher left pending, and the savepoint+commit pair is a special case siblings lack. Prefer flush() here and one commit at the boundary that already owns the run's transaction."
  },
  {
    "file": "frontend/src/components/notifications/NotificationBell.tsx",
    "line": 245,
    "summary": "\"Mark all read\" is disabled and the badge hidden whenever the count poll has not succeeded, even while the drawer lists unread entries.",
    "failure_scenario": "First GET /notifications/unread_count is 429'd/fails so unread stays null; the drawer then loads five unread items but hasUnread is false → Mark-all disabled, no badge. Reconcile unread from the loaded page when it is null, or gate the button on the page's own unread items."
```

"""The in-app notification feed (#1687): who receives a run's alert, how the entry is
written, and each user's own read state over it."""

from __future__ import annotations

import uuid
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import UTC, datetime
from typing import Any, cast

from sqlalchemy import ColumnElement, func, or_, select, update
from sqlalchemy.dialects.postgresql import insert as pg_insert
from sqlalchemy.engine import CursorResult
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

from backend.app.alerting.base import FAILING_TIERS, RunReport
from backend.app.core.config import get_settings
from backend.app.core.errors import DataQError
from backend.app.db.models import ADMIN_ROLE, Incident, Notification, Share, Suite, User

#: Failing check names listed in a body before "… and N more".
_BODY_CHECK_NAMES = 5
_TITLE_MAX = 256


class NotificationNotFoundError(DataQError):
    """The entry does not exist *or* belongs to another user — indistinguishable by
    design (404-no-leak): a feed is private to its owner.
    """

    status_code = 404
    code = "notification_not_found"


def recipients_for_suite(session: Session, suite: Suite) -> set[uuid.UUID]:
    """Every user who can see ``suite`` right now: its creator, each grantee (any level —
    a Viewer's clamp still leaves `view`), the stored-role workspace admins and the
    allowlisted ones (ADR 0033 — an allowlist admin may hold a `member` row).
    """
    emails = get_settings().workspace_admin_email_set
    admin_filter = [User.role == ADMIN_ROLE]
    if emails:
        admin_filter.append(func.lower(User.email).in_(sorted(emails)))
    recipients = set(session.scalars(select(User.id).where(or_(*admin_filter))))
    recipients.update(session.scalars(select(Share.user_id).where(Share.suite_id == suite.id)))
    if suite.created_by is not None:
        recipients.add(suite.created_by)
    return recipients


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class FeedEntry:
    """What every recipient's row says about one run — identical across users."""

    severity: str
    title: str
    body: str
    deep_link: str
    incident_id: uuid.UUID | None


def _severity(report: RunReport) -> str:
    if report.run_status == "failed":
        return "error"
    return report.worst_severity or "pass"


def compose_entry(report: RunReport) -> FeedEntry:
    """The feed text for a run, from the report the other channels already send — check
    names and counts only, so nothing an observed value or sample row would carry can
    reach the feed (the #1772 rule holds at the build step, not by later filtering).
    """
    severity = _severity(report)
    if severity == "error":
        title = f"{report.suite_name}: run failed to execute"
        body = f"The run on {report.target_label} did not complete. Open it for the reason."
    elif severity == "pass":
        title = f"{report.suite_name}: all {report.total_checks} checks passed"
        body = f"{report.target_label} — nothing breached."
    else:
        breaching = [c for c in report.checks if c.status in FAILING_TIERS]
        title = (
            f"{report.suite_name}: {len(breaching)} of {report.total_checks} checks "
            f"breached (worst: {severity})"
        )
        names = [f"{c.check_name} ({c.status})" for c in breaching[:_BODY_CHECK_NAMES]]
        more = len(breaching) - len(names)
        listed = ", ".join(names) + (f" and {more} more" if more > 0 else "")
        body = f"{report.target_label}" + (f" ({report.env})" if report.env else "") + f": {listed}"
    incident_id = report.incidents[0].incident_id if report.incidents else None
    return FeedEntry(
        severity=severity,
        title=title[:_TITLE_MAX],
        body=body,
        deep_link=f"/results/{report.run_id}",
        incident_id=incident_id,
    )


def record_run_alert(session: Session, report: RunReport) -> int:
    """Write ``report`` into every recipient's feed; return how many rows were inserted.
    Idempotent per (user, run): a re-published outcome adds nothing. Returns 0 when the
    suite is gone or nobody can see it.
    """
    suite = session.get(Suite, report.suite_id)
    if suite is None:
        return 0
    recipients = recipients_for_suite(session, suite)
    if not recipients:
        return 0
    entry = compose_entry(report)
    # The incident may have been deleted between the report build and this write; a dangling
    # FK would fail every recipient's row, so check it exists once.
    incident_id = entry.incident_id
    if incident_id is not None and session.get(Incident, incident_id) is None:
        incident_id = None
    rows = [
        {
            "user_id": user_id,
            "suite_id": report.suite_id,
            "run_id": report.run_id,
            "incident_id": incident_id,
            "severity": entry.severity,
            "title": entry.title,
            "body": entry.body,
            "deep_link": entry.deep_link,
        }
        for user_id in sorted(recipients)
    ]
    stmt = (
        pg_insert(Notification)
        .values(rows)
        .on_conflict_do_nothing(
            index_elements=["user_id", "run_id"], index_where=Notification.run_id.is_not(None)
        )
    )
    result = cast(CursorResult[Any], session.execute(stmt))
    return max(result.rowcount or 0, 0)


# ── the owner's view ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────


def _own(user_id: uuid.UUID, *, unread_only: bool) -> list[ColumnElement[bool]]:
    clauses: list[ColumnElement[bool]] = [Notification.user_id == user_id]
    if unread_only:
        clauses.append(Notification.read_at.is_(None))
    return clauses


def list_feed(
    session: Session, *, user_id: uuid.UUID, unread_only: bool, limit: int, offset: int
) -> list[tuple[Notification, uuid.UUID | None]]:
    """Newest-first page of the caller's own feed, each row paired with its incident's
    asset id (the incident deep link needs it) or ``None``.
    """
    stmt = (
        select(Notification, Incident.asset_id)
        .outerjoin(Incident, Incident.id == Notification.incident_id)
        .where(*_own(user_id, unread_only=unread_only))
        .order_by(Notification.created_at.desc(), Notification.id.desc())
        .limit(limit)
        .offset(offset)
    )
    return [(row[0], row[1]) for row in session.execute(stmt).all()]


def count_feed(session: Session, *, user_id: uuid.UUID, unread_only: bool) -> int:
    stmt = (
        select(func.count())
        .select_from(Notification)
        .where(*_own(user_id, unread_only=unread_only))
    )
    return int(session.execute(stmt).scalar_one())


def unread_count(session: Session, *, user_id: uuid.UUID) -> int:
    return count_feed(session, user_id=user_id, unread_only=True)


def mark_read(
    session: Session, *, user_id: uuid.UUID, notification_id: uuid.UUID
) -> tuple[Notification, uuid.UUID | None]:
    """Mark one of the caller's own entries read (idempotent — a second call keeps the
    first `read_at`). Another user's entry is a 404, never a 403.
    """
    row = session.execute(
        select(Notification, Incident.asset_id)
        .outerjoin(Incident, Incident.id == Notification.incident_id)
        .where(Notification.id == notification_id, Notification.user_id == user_id)
    ).first()
    if row is None:
        raise NotificationNotFoundError(
            "notification not found", detail={"notification_id": str(notification_id)}
        )
    notification, asset_id = row[0], row[1]
    if notification.read_at is None:
        notification.read_at = datetime.now(UTC)
        session.commit()
    return notification, asset_id


def mark_all_read(session: Session, *, user_id: uuid.UUID) -> int:
    """Mark every unread entry of the caller's own feed read; return how many changed."""
    result = cast(
        CursorResult[Any],
        session.execute(
            update(Notification)
            .where(Notification.user_id == user_id, Notification.read_at.is_(None))
            .values(read_at=datetime.now(UTC))
        ),
    )
    session.commit()
    return max(result.rowcount or 0, 0)


__all__ = [
    "FeedEntry",
    "NotificationNotFoundError",
    "compose_entry",
    "count_feed",
    "list_feed",
    "mark_all_read",
    "mark_read",
    "recipients_for_suite",
    "record_run_alert",
    "unread_count",
]

"""The in-app ``ResultPublisher`` (#1687): a run outcome lands in the feed of every user who
can see the suite. Runs after the same per-suite policy + routing gate as the outbound
channels; dedup and snooze were already applied before any publisher is reached
(``dispatch.publish_run_outcome``), so the feed never says what Teams/Slack/email did not.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

from backend.app.alerting.base import ConnectionHealthReport, RunReport, WorkspaceSignalReport
from backend.app.alerting.routing import route_for
from backend.app.core import usage_telemetry
from backend.app.core.logging import get_logger
from backend.app.services import notification_feed_service, notification_service

log = get_logger(__name__)


class InAppPublisher:
    """Writes a run's outcome into the recipients' feeds in the run's own session."""

    def publish(self, session: Session, report: RunReport) -> None:
        config = notification_service.get_config(session, report.suite_id)
        if config is not None and not config.enabled:
            return
        policy = config.alert_on if config is not None else notification_service.DEFAULT_ALERT_ON
        route = route_for(report, policy)
        if not route.should_send:
            return
        try:
            # A savepoint: a failed insert must not leave the worker's session in an aborted
            # transaction for the channels and hooks that run after this one.
            with session.begin_nested():
                inserted = notification_feed_service.record_run_alert(session, report)
            session.commit()
        except Exception:
            # Named here (the composite logs the generic `channel_publish_failed` with the
            # traceback) so a feed-only outage is searchable on its own; then re-raised so
            # the composite's isolation and logging apply unchanged.
            log.warning("inapp_feed_write_failed", run_id=str(report.run_id))
            raise
        if inserted == 0:
            # Re-publish of an outcome already in every feed (worker retry), or a suite nobody
            # can see — neither is a delivery, so no telemetry event.
            log.info("inapp_alert_skipped", run_id=str(report.run_id), suite=report.suite_name)
            return
        usage_telemetry.emit(
            usage_telemetry.UsageEvent.ALERT_DELIVERED, session=session, channel="in_app"
        )
        log.info(
            "inapp_alert_recorded",
            run_id=str(report.run_id),
            suite=report.suite_name,
            recipients=inserted,
            worst_severity=report.worst_severity,
            urgency=route.urgency,
        )

    def publish_health(self, session: Session, report: ConnectionHealthReport) -> bool:
        """Not delivered here: a connection-health edge has no suite, and the feed is scoped
        by suite grants. ``False`` so the caller's delivered-first flag is never stamped by a
        channel that wrote nothing (#1101).
        """
        return False

    def publish_workspace_signal(self, session: Session, report: WorkspaceSignalReport) -> bool:
        """Not delivered here — same reason as :meth:`publish_health`."""
        return False

        names = [f"{c.check_name} ({c.status})" for c in breaching[:_BODY_CHECK_NAMES]]
        more = len(breaching) - len(names)
        listed = ", ".join(names) + (f" and {more} more" if more > 0 else "")
        body = f"{report.target_label}" + (f" ({report.env})" if report.env else "") + f": {listed}"
    incident_id = report.incidents[0].incident_id if report.incidents else None
    return FeedEntry(
        severity=severity,
        title=title[:_TITLE_MAX],
        body=body,
        deep_link=f"/results/{report.run_id}",
        incident_id=incident_id,
    )


def record_run_alert(session: Session, report: RunReport) -> int:
    """Write ``report`` into every recipient's feed; return how many rows were inserted.
    Idempotent per (user, run): a re-published outcome adds nothing. Returns 0 when the
    suite is gone or nobody can see it.
    """
    suite = session.get(Suite, report.suite_id)
    if suite is None:
        return 0
    recipients = recipients_for_suite(session, suite)
    if not recipients:
        return 0
    entry = compose_entry(report)
    # The incident may have been deleted between the report build and this write; a dangling
    # FK would fail every recipient's row, so check it exists once.
    incident_id = entry.incident_id
    if incident_id is not None and session.get(Incident, incident_id) is None:
        incident_id = None
    rows = [
        {
            "user_id": user_id,
            "suite_id": report.suite_id,
            "run_id": report.run_id,
            "incident_id": incident_id,
            "severity": entry.severity,
            "title": entry.title,
            "body": entry.body,
            "deep_link": entry.deep_link,
        }
        for user_id in sorted(recipients)
    ]
    stmt = (
        pg_insert(Notification)
        .values(rows)
        .on_conflict_do_nothing(
            index_elements=["user_id", "run_id"], index_where=Notification.run_id.is_not(None)
        )
    )
    result = cast(CursorResult[Any], session.execute(stmt))
    return max(result.rowcount or 0, 0)


# ── the owner's view ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────


def _own(user_id: uuid.UUID, *, unread_only: bool) -> list[ColumnElement[bool]]:
    clauses: list[ColumnElement[bool]] = [Notification.user_id == user_id]
    if unread_only:
        clauses.append(Notification.read_at.is_(None))
    return clauses


def list_feed(
    session: Session, *, user_id: uuid.UUID, unread_only: bool, limit: int, offset: int
) -> list[tuple[Notification, uuid.UUID | None]]:
    """Newest-first page of the caller's own feed, each row paired with its incident's
    asset id (the incident deep link needs it) or ``None``.
    """
    stmt = (
        select(Notification, Incident.asset_id)
        .outerjoin(Incident, Incident.id == Notification.incident_id)
        .where(*_own(user_id, unread_only=unread_only))
        .order_by(Notification.created_at.desc(), Notification.id.desc())
        .limit(limit)
        .offset(offset)
    )
    return [(row[0], row[1]) for row in session.execute(stmt).all()]


def count_feed(session: Session, *, user_id: uuid.UUID, unread_only: bool) -> int:
    stmt = (
        select(func.count())
        .select_from(Notification)
        .where(*_own(user_id, unread_only=unread_only))
    )
    return int(session.execute(stmt).scalar_one())


def unread_count(session: Session, *, user_id: uuid.UUID) -> int:
    return count_feed(session, user_id=user_id, unread_only=True)


def mark_read(
    session: Session, *, user_id: uuid.UUID, notification_id: uuid.UUID
) -> tuple[Notification, uuid.UUID | None]:
    """Mark one of the caller's own entries read (idempotent — a second call keeps the
    first `read_at`). Another user's entry is a 404, never a 403.
    """
    row = session.execute(
        select(Notification, Incident.asset_id)
        .outerjoin(Incident, Incident.id == Notification.incident_id)
        .where(Notification.id == notification_id, Notification.user_id == user_id)
    ).first()
    if row is None:
        raise NotificationNotFoundError(
            "notification not found", detail={"notification_id": str(notification_id)}
        )
    notification, asset_id = row[0], row[1]
    if notification.read_at is None:
        notification.read_at = datetime.now(UTC)
        session.commit()
    return notification, asset_id


def mark_all_read(session: Session, *, user_id: uuid.UUID) -> int:
    """Mark every unread entry of the caller's own feed read; return how many changed."""
    result = cast(
        CursorResult[Any],
        session.execute(
            update(Notification)
            .where(Notification.user_id == user_id, Notification.read_at.is_(None))
            .values(read_at=datetime.now(UTC))
        ),
    )
    session.commit()
    return max(result.rowcount or 0, 0)

log = get_logger(__name__)


class InAppPublisher:
    """Writes a run's outcome into the recipients' feeds in the run's own session."""

    def publish(self, session: Session, report: RunReport) -> None:
        config = notification_service.get_config(session, report.suite_id)
        if config is not None and not config.enabled:
            return
        policy = config.alert_on if config is not None else notification_service.DEFAULT_ALERT_ON
        route = route_for(report, policy)
        if not route.should_send:
            return
        try:
            # A savepoint: a failed insert must not leave the worker's session in an aborted
            # transaction for the channels and hooks that run after this one.
            with session.begin_nested():
                inserted = notification_feed_service.record_run_alert(session, report)
            session.commit()
        except Exception:
            # Named here (the composite logs the generic `channel_publish_failed` with the
            # traceback) so a feed-only outage is searchable on its own; then re-raised so
            # the composite's isolation and logging apply unchanged.
            log.warning("inapp_feed_write_failed", run_id=str(report.run_id))
            raise
        if inserted == 0:
            # Re-publish of an outcome already in every feed (worker retry), or a suite nobody
            # can see — neither is a delivery, so no telemetry event.
            log.info("inapp_alert_skipped", run_id=str(report.run_id), suite=report.suite_name)
            return
        usage_telemetry.emit(
            usage_telemetry.UsageEvent.ALERT_DELIVERED, session=session, channel="in_app"
        )
        log.info(
            "inapp_alert_recorded",
            run_id=str(report.run_id),
            suite=report.suite_name,
            recipients=inserted,
            worst_severity=report.worst_severity,
            urgency=route.urgency,
        )

        """Not delivered here: a connection-health edge has no suite, and the feed is scoped
        by suite grants. ``False`` so the caller's delivered-first flag is never stamped by a
        channel that wrote nothing (#1101).
        """
        return False

    def publish_workspace_signal(self, session: Session, report: WorkspaceSignalReport) -> bool:
        """Not delivered here — same reason as :meth:`publish_health`."""

    try:

        if run is None or run.status not in _PUBLISHABLE_STATUSES:
            return False
        # Suppress when every failing check is snoozed (the operator silenced them); a partial
        # snooze still alerts on the live checks.
        if suppression.all_failures_snoozed(session, run):

        # shouldn't re-alert every run (a clean run is never a "duplicate", so this is a no-op for
        # the passing path).
        config = notification_service.get_config(session, run.suite_id)
        policy = config.alert_on if (config is not None and config.enabled) else None

    @property
    def success(self) -> bool:
        """Data-quality verdict: the run executed cleanly *and* nothing breached.
        Derived (not stored) so it can never drift from ``worst_severity`` — the
        same drift-free pattern as the count properties below.
        """
        return self.run_status == "succeeded" and self.worst_severity is None

    @property
    def total_checks(self) -> int:
        return sum(self.counts.values())

    @property
    def failed_checks(self) -> int:
        """Checks that genuinely breached (``fail`` + ``critical``) — ``warn`` is
        surfaced via ``worst_severity``, not counted as a failure here.
        """
        return self.counts.get("fail", 0) + self.counts.get("critical", 0)

    @property
    def has_failures(self) -> bool:
        """Alert-worthy: the run couldn't execute, or any check breached a tier
        (incl. ``warn``). Publishers/routing refine *whether* to send on top of
        this (severity-aware routing + the per-suite on-fail/warn/always policy).
        """
        return self.run_status == "failed" or any(
            self.counts.get(tier, 0) for tier in FAILING_TIERS
        )

- **Check version history** — every edit is versioned and viewable per check.

## Suites

A **suite** is a named set of checks bound to one connection + target
([Datasources & checks](datasources-checks.md)):

- **Run target** — one table (SQL) or one file/batch (flat file) per suite.
- **Sharing** — per-suite **view / edit** grants (suite-level is the access model; no
  folder scopes). See [access & auth](#access-auth).
- **Export / import** — move a suite's definition between environments (author on DEV,
  import against PROD) instead of re-clicking checks.

## Running checks

## Tags

A **tag** is a short workspace-shared label — `finance`, `team:core-data`, `tier-1` — that
can sit on a suite, an asset, a connection or a check. The vocabulary is one list for the
whole workspace; assigning a tag to something you can edit is enough to create it, and a name
is stored lower-case, trimmed and single-spaced, so `Finance` and `finance` are one tag.

- **Where they show.** As chips on the Suites, Assets and Connections lists and on a suite's
  check rows; the Suites and Assets lists have a **Tags (all of)** filter, which keeps only the
  rows carrying every chosen tag (the API's repeatable `tag=` query parameter, AND semantics).
- **Who can assign.** The same people who can edit the thing: a suite's or check's tags need
  edit on the suite, a connection's or an asset's tags need the workspace Admin role. Everyone
  who can see an entity sees its tags; nobody can list a suite's tags they could not open.
- **Deleting.** Deleting a suite, asset, connection or check drops its assignments with it.
  Deleting a tag (Admin, `DELETE /tags/{id}`) detaches it everywhere at once; `GET /tags`
  lists the vocabulary with a usage count per entity kind, so an unused tag is easy to find.
- **Not a classification.** Tags are user labels. A column's PII classification comes from the
  column policy and from warehouse-native tags ([data protection](#data-protection)), never
  from a DataQ tag.
'''),
])
edit('docs/site/guides/best-practices.md', [
('''## Severity: make the tiers mean something''','''## Tag by domain and criticality, not by state

one: the owning domain or team (`finance`, `team:core-data`), the criticality (`tier-1`) and
perhaps the consumer (`exec-dashboard`). Keep a `key:value` shape for anything that will have
more than a handful of values. Do not encode state that the app already tracks — a suite's
environment, its health, whether it is scheduled — a tag goes stale the moment the fact
changes, and the lists already filter by the real thing. Names are normalised (lower-case,
trimmed), so agree spellings once; `GET /tags` shows the vocabulary with usage counts when it
is time to prune.

## Severity: make the tiers mean something'''),
])

can sit on a suite, an asset, a connection or a check. The vocabulary is one list for the
whole workspace; assigning a tag to something you can edit is enough to create it, and a name
is stored lower-case, trimmed and single-spaced, so `Finance` and `finance` are one tag.

- **Where they show.** As chips on the Suites, Assets and Connections lists and on a suite's
  check rows; the Suites and Assets lists have a **Tags (all of)** filter, which keeps only the
  rows carrying every chosen tag (the API's repeatable `tag=` query parameter, AND semantics).
- **Who can assign.** The same people who can edit the thing: a suite's or check's tags need
  edit on the suite, a connection's or an asset's tags need the workspace Admin role. Everyone
  who can see an entity sees its tags; nobody can list a suite's tags they could not open.
- **Deleting.** Deleting a suite, asset, connection or check drops its assignments with it.
  Deleting a tag (Admin, `DELETE /tags/{id}`) detaches it everywhere at once; `GET /tags`
  lists the vocabulary with a usage count per entity kind, so an unused tag is easy to find.
- **Not a classification.** Tags are user labels. A column's PII classification comes from the
  column policy and from warehouse-native tags ([data protection](#data-protection)), never
  from a DataQ tag.
'''),

 * about what the form says now" from "this answer is about what the form said 300ms ago".
 */
type BatchPreviewSpec = string;

type BatchPreviewState =
  | { status: 'idle' }
  | { status: 'loading'; spec: BatchPreviewSpec }
  | {
      status: 'resolved';
      spec: BatchPreviewSpec;
      path: string;
      truncated: boolean;
      scanned: number;
    }
  | { status: 'no-match'; spec: BatchPreviewSpec; truncated: boolean; scanned: number }
  | { status: 'error'; spec: BatchPreviewSpec; message: string };

lines: # steward's recorded decision — sweeping the asset would erase it silently, and the column
# would re-mask on the next profile with no trace of ever having been cleared.
+    # #888: a tag is a steward's label, applied by hand — an asset someone tagged is never
+    # swept, or the label would vanish with the row and nothing would say why.
- **Who can assign.** The same people who can edit the thing: a suite's or check's tags need
edit on the suite, a connection's or an asset's tags need the workspace Admin role. Everyone
who can see an entity sees its tags; nobody can list a suite's tags they could not open.
+- **A tag pins an asset.** The orphan-asset sweep never removes an asset that carries a tag,
+  even when no suite, run or lineage edge references it any more — a label is a decision
+  someone made, and the Assets list is where it is kept.
- **Deleting.** Deleting a suite, asset, connection or check drops its assignments with it.
Deleting a tag (Admin, `DELETE /tags/{id}`) detaches it everywhere at once; `GET /tags`
lists the vocabulary with a usage count per entity kind, so an unused tag is easy to find.

    def visit_Assert(self,node):

def test_update_check_leaves_omitted_fields_alone(db_session: Any, monkeypatch: Any) -> None:
    """PATCH semantics: omission means "unchanged", not "clear". The tool docstring
    tells an LLM this outright, because the natural repair for a field it wants
    gone — passing 0 or "" — would SET that value, not remove it.
    """
    user = _user(db_session)
    suite = _suite(db_session, user)
    check = _check(db_session, suite, dimension="completeness", warn_threshold=Decimal("0.01"))
    _as(monkeypatch, db_session, user)

    out = server.update_check(str(suite.id), str(check.id), name="renamed")
    assert out["name"] == "renamed"
    assert out["warn_threshold"] == 0.01
    assert out["dimension"] == "completeness"
    assert out["config"] == {"column": "EMAIL"}

{"body":"## Idea
Allow a suite to be triggered by the **completion of another suite** (DQ gating / sequential dependencies): e.g. run downstream suite B only after upstream suite A passes.

## Why it's deferred (not in v1)
DataQ's trigger model is `trigger_bindings`: `(provider, pipeline_or_dag_id, env) → suite_id` — a suite runs on an **orchestration pipeline/DAG** completion (ADF/Airflow), never on another suite. Sequencing/dependencies are intentionally the **orchestrator's** job (CLAUDE.md §4): the orchestrator owns the workflow DAG and chains steps; DataQ observes completion and triggers checks. Suite→suite chaining would make DataQ a mini-orchestrator, which it deliberately is not.

Today's real-world equivalent: put both suites' triggers on the same pipeline, or let the orchestrator sequence the upstream/downstream jobs.

## Why it's plausible post-v1
`trigger_bindings` is provider-agnostic, and ADR 0011 already imagines non-Azure trigger sources (even dbt-as-`OrchestrationProvider`). A **"DataQ suite" could itself become a trigger `provider`** — a suite run reaching a terminal state emits a completion event that fires bindings keyed on `provider='suite'`, `pipeline_or_dag_id=<suite_id>`. This slots into the existing abstraction without a schema rewrite.

## Open questions
- Only trigger on **pass**, or on any terminal state (with a status predicate)?
- Cycle detection (A→B→A) and fan-out depth limits.
- Whether this belongs in DataQ at all vs. documenting the orchestrator-chaining pattern.

Captured from a product discussion; revisit post-v1 alongside the Suite Triggers UI (#216).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `trigger_bindings` supports suite-on-suite (run suite B when suite A completes successfully)
- [ ] Cycle/self-trigger protection enforced + tested; UI can author the binding

"""The `runs.triggered_by` ↔ `pipeline_runs` correlation, in ONE place (#1728).

`orchestration_service._trigger_suites` stamps a triggered run with
``f"{provider}:{pipeline_or_dag_id}:{provider_run_id}"``. Neither id is colon-free
(an Airflow ``run_id`` carries timestamps, dbt's job_name is free-form webhook
input), so the marker cannot be split back apart — and two distinct pipeline runs
can reconstruct to the identical string when a colon lands on the other side of
the boundary (``"nightly:etl"``+``"run-1"`` vs ``"nightly"``+``"etl:run-1"``).
Every reader therefore reconstructs-and-compares against the stored columns and
FAILS CLOSED when more than one row matches (#1714), instead of attributing a DQ
run to whichever row came back first.

Both directions are indexed (#1715): marker -> `pipeline_runs` by the
`ix_pipeline_runs_marker` expression index (#1814), marker -> `runs` by
`ix_runs_triggered_by`. Neither index can be made UNIQUE — a colliding marker is
legitimate input, and a unique index would refuse the INSERT instead of letting
the reader fail closed.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import uuid
from collections.abc import Collection, Iterable, Sequence
from dataclasses import dataclass, field

from sqlalchemy import ColumnElement, Select, func, select
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

from backend.app.core.logging import get_logger

# ADR 0046 — Pipeline DQ gate: an orchestrator asks DataQ whether to continue

- **Status:** Accepted (2026-09-29)
- **Date:** 2026-09-29
- **Deciders:** @TheurgicDuke771
- **Related:** ADR [0005](0005-severity-tier-weights.md) / [0016](0016-severity-derivation-semantics.md) (severity ladder), [0026](0026-auth-api-keys-and-principal-seam.md) (PATs), [0027](0027-suite-permission-model-workspace-admin.md) (per-suite `view`/`edit`), [0035](0035-request-rate-limiting.md) (rate limits); ADR [0004](0004-orchestration-abstraction.md) (the `OrchestrationProvider` contract this extends).

## Context

Orchestration providers (ADF, Airflow, dbt) have exactly three responsibilities in DataQ:
**monitor** runs, **detect failure**, and **trigger** bound suites when a pipeline run
**succeeds**. None of them lets a pipeline act on a DQ verdict. The proven feature in this
market is a *circuit breaker*: a pipeline stage asks "did the data pass?" and halts its own
downstream stages on a breach.

A read-only "did the suite triggered for my run pass?" endpoint would not work for the
common case. Suites are triggered when a pipeline run **completes**, so a stage in the
**middle** of a run would be waiting for a trigger that cannot fire until the run it is
blocking finishes.

## Decision

1. **A fourth responsibility: answer a gate request.** DataQ still never mutates a pipeline.
   The customer's DAG or pipeline chooses to call DataQ and to wait or fail on the answer.
   The gate is provider-agnostic: it is keyed by the existing `trigger_bindings`
   (`provider`, `pipeline_or_dag_id`, `env`) and has no provider-specific branch.
2. **One endpoint, two modes:** `POST /api/v1/orchestration/gate` with
   `provider`, `pipeline_or_dag_id`, `env`, `provider_run_id`, `fail_on`
   (`warn` | `fail` | `critical`, default `fail`) and `trigger` (default `true`).
   - **Trigger-and-wait** (`trigger: true`): DataQ ensures one run of every enabled bound
     suite exists for this pipeline run and returns its current state. The run carries the
     same `triggered_by` marker the success-event path uses
     (`<provider>:<pipeline_or_dag_id>:<provider_run_id>`), so the existing partial unique
     index makes it **idempotent**: repeated polls, and the run's own later success event,
     never start a second run. Polling the same request until a terminal state is the
     intended client loop.
   - **Status only** (`trigger: false`): DataQ creates nothing. It reports on runs that
     already exist for the marker, e.g. a downstream pipeline gating on an upstream run
     that the normal success event triggered.
3. **States, never a bare boolean:** `awaiting_trigger` (status-only, no run yet),
   `running` (any bound run queued or running), `passed`, `failed` (some result at or above
   `fail_on`), `error` (a run failed operationally or was cancelled, or a check could not be
   evaluated). The response lists each bound suite's run, status, worst severity and counts,
   plus a `retry_after_seconds` hint. `error` is distinct from `failed` so a client can
   choose; the shipped snippets **fail closed** on both.

    session: Session,
    *,
    provider: str,

    enabled: bool = True,
) -> BindingResult:
    """Create a binding. Requires `edit` on the target suite (404/403 otherwise)."""
    _validate_provider_env(provider, env)
    # Proves the suite exists (404) and the caller may automate it (403).
    require_permission(session, suite_id, user_id, minimum="edit")

    binding = TriggerBinding(
        provider=provider,
        pipeline_or_dag_id=pipeline_or_dag_id,
        env=env,
        suite_id=suite_id,
        enabled=enabled,
    )
    session.add(binding)
    try:
        # Inside the try: `record_entity_change` flushes to obtain the server-assigned id, which is
        # where the duplicate-binding unique constraint now fires.
        audit_service.record_entity_change(

            entity_type="trigger_binding",
            entity=binding,
            actor=user_id,
        )
        session.commit()
    except IntegrityError as exc:
        session.rollback()
        raise TriggerBindingConflictError(
            "a binding for this (provider, pipeline, env, suite) already exists",

) -> list[TriggerBinding]:

# ADR 0051 — Suite-on-suite triggers: a suite's own success as a trigger provider

- **Status:** Proposed (2026-10-25)
- **Date:** 2026-10-25
- **Deciders:** @TheurgicDuke771
- **Related:** ADR [0004](0004-orchestration-abstraction.md) (the `OrchestrationProvider` contract), [0011](0011-provider-agnostic-trigger-bindings.md) (`trigger_bindings` as the provider-agnostic trigger key), [0029](0029-dbt-orchestration-provider.md) (the last time the provider value-set widened), [0046](0046-pipeline-dq-gate.md) (the gate, which this does **not** extend), [0027](0027-suite-permission-model-workspace-admin.md) (per-suite `view`/`edit`).

## Context

A suite runs today on a schedule, by hand, or when a bound **orchestration** pipeline or DAG
succeeds. Issue #244 asks for the fourth source: run suite B when suite A has run and passed —
a downstream dataset's checks only make sense once the upstream dataset has been verified, and
two suites bound to the same pipeline run in parallel, not in order.

The reason it was deferred stands: DataQ is not an orchestrator. Sequencing work is the
orchestrator's job (CLAUDE.md §4), and a suite that fans out into a graph of suites is a
mini-DAG DataQ would then have to schedule, retry and visualise. The customer's orchestrator
already does all of that. What it cannot do is express "when **DataQ** says the upstream is
good"; the gate (ADR 0046) covers that for a pipeline stage, but not for a suite that has no
pipeline of its own — a suite on a flat-file landing zone, a reconciliation suite that should
follow the two suites it reconciles.

`trigger_bindings` is `(provider, pipeline_or_dag_id, env) → suite_id` and is already
provider-agnostic; the only provider-specific part of a trigger is who **observes** the
completion. For an orchestrator that is a webhook or a poll; for a suite it is DataQ itself,
at the moment the run reaches its terminal state. Nothing else in the chain —
`insert_triggered_run`, the `triggered_by` marker, the dedup index, dispatch — cares where the
event came from.

## Decision

1. **A suite is a trigger provider, not an orchestration provider.** `provider = 'suite'`
   joins a new `TRIGGER_PROVIDERS` value-set (`adf`, `airflow`, `dbt`, `suite`) that governs
   `trigger_bindings.provider`, binding validation and the `triggered_by` dedup predicate.
   `ORCHESTRATION_PROVIDERS` is **unchanged**: there is no `suite` connection type, no
   `pipeline_runs` row, no poller, no webhook, no health signal, and the gate endpoint
   (ADR 0046) refuses `provider='suite'` — a suite chain has no pipeline stage to answer.
2. **The binding key.** `pipeline_or_dag_id` holds the **upstream suite's id**; `env` must
   equal the upstream suite's connection env and is filled in by the server, so the firing
   lookup stays the one every provider uses: `(provider, pipeline_or_dag_id, env, enabled)`.
3. **When it fires: success only, by default and for now.** A run fires its bindings when it
   reaches `succeeded` with no check at `fail` or `critical` (a `warn` passes, an `error`ed or
   skipped check does not block — the run still verified what it could). A run that `failed`,
   was `cancelled`, or has a breach fires nothing; the downstream suite is not run against
   data the upstream just said was bad. A per-binding `fire_on` predicate is deliberately not
   added until someone asks for it with a case: the "run B on A's failure" shape is an alert,
   which notifications already deliver.
4. **The marker.** The downstream run carries `triggered_by = 'suite:<upstream_suite_id>:<upstream_run_id>'`.
   Both ids are UUIDs, so unlike every orchestrator marker this one **can** be split — but
   readers still go through `orchestration.markers`, and the partial unique index
   `uq_runs_suite_triggered_by` (predicate widened to `suite:%`) makes a re-fired completion
   (a worker retry, a reaper flipping a stuck run) a no-op, exactly as for pipeline events.
5. **Guards, at authoring and at firing.**
   - *Self:* a suite cannot be bound to itself (422).
   - *Cycle:* creating a binding that would make the upstream reachable from the downstream
     through enabled **or disabled** suite bindings is refused (422, naming the path). Disabled
     ones count because `enabled` is a toggle, not a deletion, and re-enabling must not be the
     moment a cycle appears.
   - *Depth:* at firing time a chain deeper than `SUITE_TRIGGER_MAX_DEPTH` (5) stops and logs
     `suite_trigger_depth_exceeded` instead of running — the depth is read back through the
     markers, so a cycle that slipped past authoring (two bindings created in the same instant)
     is bounded as well. Fan-out width is unbounded: one upstream may trigger many suites.
   - *Access:* creating or enabling the binding needs `edit` on the downstream suite (today's
     rule) **and** `view` on the upstream suite — you cannot chain onto a suite you cannot
     see, which would otherwise be an enumeration channel for suite ids.
6. **Where it fires.** In the worker, after the run's terminal commit and the alert dispatch
   (`run_suite` in `worker/tasks.py`): `suite_trigger_service.fire_for_run`, fail-soft like
   the hooks beside it (a broken trigger never fails the run that completed). It reuses
   `insert_triggered_run` + `run_dispatch.dispatch_or_fail`, so the downstream run is queued
   through the same admission and the same broker-down handling as a pipeline-triggered one.
7. **What the user sees.** The Triggers panel offers "Another suite (on success)" beside the
   orchestrators, with a suite picker (suites the user can see) in place of the free-text
   pipeline id and the env filled from the chosen suite. A triggered run's label reads
   "Suite — <upstream suite name>" and links to the upstream run. MCP `create_trigger_binding`
   / `list_trigger_bindings` accept and return `provider='suite'`, with the docstrings saying
   what fires it and what never does.

## Consequences

- No migration beyond widening two value-sets: the `trigger_bindings` provider CHECK and the
  `uq_runs_suite_triggered_by` predicate (the same shape as ADR 0029's dbt widening, and
  reversible until the first `suite` binding exists).
- DataQ gains a one-hop dependency, not a DAG: it never retries, reorders or visualises a
  chain, and the depth cap keeps a mistaken loop from becoming a runaway. Anyone who needs a
  real DAG keeps using the orchestrator, which can now **gate** on DataQ (ADR 0046) and bind
  suites to its stages; this ADR is for the suites that have no stage.
- `incident_evidence`'s upstream-pipeline layer stays pipeline-only (`ORCHESTRATION_PROVIDERS`);
  a `suite:` marker yields no pipeline layer, which is correct — there is no pipeline.
- Near-miss detection (#1186) does not apply: the env is derived, never typed.

## Alternatives considered

- **Document the orchestrator-chaining pattern and build nothing.** Rejected for the suites
  that have no orchestrator stage (landing-zone files, reconciliation suites). The pattern
  is still the recommendation when a stage exists, and the guide says so.
- **Add `suite` to `ORCHESTRATION_PROVIDERS`.** Rejected: eighteen call sites would then
  treat it as a connection type with a poller, a webhook secret, a health signal and a
  `pipeline_runs` history, none of which exist.
- **A `fire_on` predicate per binding (`passed` | `any_terminal`).** Deferred (decision 3).
- **Cycle checks at firing time only.** Rejected: a user should learn about a loop when they
  make it, not when the chain runs at 03:00; firing-time depth remains as the backstop.

    provider: str,
    # Same bound as the REST twin: the column is String(256) NOT NULL, and an
    # empty value would create a binding that can never match a pipeline.
    pipeline_or_dag_id: Annotated[str, Field(min_length=1, max_length=256)],
    env: str,
    suite_id: str,
    enabled: bool = True,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Run a suite automatically whenever an orchestrator pipeline succeeds.

    Use this for 'run the orders checks after the nightly load finishes'. Binds
    pipeline/DAG ``pipeline_or_dag_id`` on ``provider`` (adf / airflow / dbt) in
    environment ``env`` to this suite: when that pipeline **completes
    successfully** in that environment, the suite runs.

    Only success triggers a run. A pipeline *failure* alerts but never triggers —
    do not offer this as a way to react to failures.

    ``env`` is part of the key and is the commonest thing to get wrong: a binding
    on ``dev`` never fires for a pipeline whose runs are reported against ``qa``.
    Any returned ``warnings`` are advisory, not errors — read them out, because
    they name exactly that class of silent no-fire. But an **empty** ``warnings``
    does not mean the wiring is sound: no ambiguity check runs at all when the
    binding is created disabled, and if no orchestration connection exists for
    this provider and environment, DataQ never observes that pipeline and the
    binding can never fire. Check ``list_connections(type=provider, env=env)``
    before telling the user it is wired. When they later report the suite did not
    run, ``get_near_misses`` shows the mismatches actually observed.

    **An "already exists" error does not mean the trigger works.** The uniqueness
    key is provider + pipeline + environment + suite and does **not** include
    ``enabled``, so a *disabled* binding collides here exactly like a live one. If
    you get that error while wiring something up, check
    ``list_trigger_bindings`` and, if the existing one is disabled, enable it with
    ``update_trigger_binding`` — otherwise you will report the trigger as in place
    when it never fires. Requires edit access.
    """
    sid = _parse_uuid(suite_id, field="suite_id")
    # NUL can't be stored by Postgres and the driver's ValueError would escape
    # `_service_errors` — the same boundary rejection every other free-text tool
    # argument gets (#567).
    if contains_nul({"pipeline_or_dag_id": pipeline_or_dag_id, "provider": provider, "env": env}):

            enabled=enabled,

        return {

            "provider": result.binding.provider,
            "pipeline_or_dag_id": result.binding.pipeline_or_dag_id,

            "enabled": result.binding.enabled,

=== features.md orchestration section
## Orchestration (monitor + trigger only)

DataQ **observes** pipelines and triggers suites on success — it never runs them, and these
are **not** datasources ([Orchestration](orchestration.md)):

- **Azure Data Factory** — Azure Monitor alert → webhook (+ 10-min poll).

    _, _, run_text = rest.partition(":")
    try:

def chain_depth(session: Session, run: Run) -> int:
    """How many suite-triggered hops led to ``run`` (0 for a run nothing in DataQ triggered)."""
    depth = 0

        current = session.get(Run, parent_id)

    manual = _run(db_session, suites[0], "pass", marker=f"manual:{owner.id}")
    hop1 = _run(db_session, suites[1], "pass", marker=f"suite:{suites[0].id}:{manual.id}")
    hop2 = _run(db_session, suites[2], "pass", marker=f"suite:{suites[1].id}:{hop1.id}")
    assert svc.chain_depth(db_session, manual) == 0
    assert svc.chain_depth(db_session, hop1) == 1

def test_a_chain_at_the_depth_cap_stops(db_session: Any) -> None:
    owner = _user(db_session)
    conn = _connection(db_session, owner)
    suites = [_suite(db_session, owner, conn) for _ in range(SUITE_TRIGGER_MAX_DEPTH + 2)]
    for upstream, downstream in zip(suites, suites[1:], strict=False):
        _bind(db_session, upstream=upstream, downstream=downstream)
    db_session.commit()
    # Runs 0..MAX already exist as a chain; run MAX is the one whose followers would be hop MAX+1.
    previous = _run(db_session, suites[0], "pass", marker=f"manual:{owner.id}")
    for i in range(1, SUITE_TRIGGER_MAX_DEPTH + 1):

    assert _downstream_runs(db_session, suites[-1]) == []
    # One hop below the cap still fires.
    below = db_session.get(Run, previous.id)
    assert below is not None
    hop_before = db_session.scalars(
        select(Run).where(Run.suite_id == suites[SUITE_TRIGGER_MAX_DEPTH - 1].id)
    ).one()
    assert svc.fire_for_run(db_session, run_id=hop_before.id) == []  # its follower already exists
    assert int(db_session.scalar(select(func.count()).select_from(Run))) == SUITE_TRIGGER_MAX_DEPTH + 1

    suites = [_suite(db_session, owner, conn) for _ in range(SUITE_TRIGGER_MAX_DEPTH + 2)]
    for upstream, downstream in zip(suites, suites[1:], strict=False):
        _bind(db_session, upstream=upstream, downstream=downstream)
    db_session.commit()
    # Runs 0..MAX already exist as a chain; run MAX is the one whose followers would be hop MAX+1.
    previous = _run(db_session, suites[0], "pass", marker=f"manual:{owner.id}")
    for i in range(1, SUITE_TRIGGER_MAX_DEPTH + 1):
        previous = _run(
            db_session, suites[i], "pass", marker=f"suite:{suites[i - 1].id}:{previous.id}"
        )

    assert svc.fire_for_run(db_session, run_id=previous.id) == []

    # One hop below the cap still fires.
    below = db_session.get(Run, previous.id)

    hop_before = db_session.scalars(
        select(Run).where(Run.suite_id == suites[SUITE_TRIGGER_MAX_DEPTH - 1].id)
    ).one()
    assert svc.fire_for_run(db_session, run_id=hop_before.id) == []  # its follower already exists
    assert int(db_session.scalar(select(func.count()).select_from(Run))) == SUITE_TRIGGER_MAX_DEPTH + 1
